title: version-to-contract-manifest-and-graded-canary-playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a deterministic, terraform-first control plane versioning flow and an automated graded canary playbook for private (VPC) deployments. Deliverables include an IaC manifest format (version-contract), Terraform modules and guards that publish a version manifest, a gating service that enforces plan/holdpoints, and a telemetry-driven promotion/rollback engine that integrates with Console SLO signals.
background: We currently rely on manual orchestration and ad-hoc scripts for private control plane upgrades. That pattern causes variable lead times, inconsistent tenant selection, and limited observability during small cohort promotions. With more private customers and stricter SLAs we need an automated pipeline that: (1) encodes version-to-contract guarantees so runtime/operators know compatibility constraints, (2) lets infrastructure teams author upgrades via Terraform without running imperative scripts, and (3) performs small, measurable graded canaries with automated promotion/rollback based on health signals.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform modules produce a signed JSON "version-contract" manifest artifact and publish it to a controlled bucket or registry
Plan-time validation: terraform plan shows any contract-breaking changes and fails gating when constraints are violated
A stateless gating service consumes manifests and pushes rollout intents to the controlplane controller; rollout intents include cohort slices and throttles
Canary rollout engine performs a staged promotion (1%, 5%, 25%, 100%) with automated checks at each step driven by p50/p95 latency, error-rate, and reconciliation lag metrics
Rollback is automatic when configured thresholds are breached; rollback path is tested in CI and has an operator manual override
End-to-end e2e test that runs in a staging VPC: apply terraform, verify manifest published, run canary promotion, intentionally inject a degraded metric and confirm rollback
Runbook and Console dashboards updated: rollout timeline, per-cohort latency/errors, token-level cost delta, and audit trail for promoted versions
tasks: Design version-contract schema (fields: semantic_version, required_api_semver, feature_flags, supported_node_pools, min_operator_version, upgrade_timing_hint, signed_by)
Implement Terraform module `redwood/controlplane_version_manifest` that builds and signs the manifest and exposes an output URI
Add terraform plan-time check hook that validates contract compatibility using terraform external data / sentinel-like hook
Build gating service (stateless lambda/service) that watches manifests and creates RolloutIntent CRs in the private controlplane cluster
Enhance controlplane operator to accept RolloutIntent CR with cohort definitions and throttles; operator performs tenant slicing and progressive promotion
Integrate Console metrics to observe p50/p95 latency, reconciler backlog, pod restarts, operator errors and expose promotion decision metrics
Create automated e2e tests and a chaos test that simulates a 503 spike to verify rollback behaves correctly
Document runbook: preflight checklist, promotion thresholds, rollback steps, emergency-only forced-promote procedure
rollout_plan: T+0: Merge terraform module and gating service behind feature flag; publish to internal registry
T+1: Smoke deploy gating service and module to staging; run demo apply to staging VPC to produce manifest
T+2: Enable operator consumption of RolloutIntent in staging; run 4-stage canary with synthetic traffic and metric probes
T+3: Validate e2e and chaos tests; iterate on threshold tuning (p95 latency, error-rate windows)
T+4: Soft launch to a small subset of private customers via opt-in flag and manual approval step in Console
T+5: After 2 successful real-customer promotions and no regressions for 72h, unflag and open to regular private upgrades
notes: Tradeoffs: pushing manifest signing into Terraform improves immutability but increases TF state coupling — mitigated by storing only manifest URI and signature in state and publishing artifact outside TF state bucket
Tenant selection: prefer deterministic hashing of tenant ID -> cohort slice to ensure reproducible promotion and easier blast-radius reasoning
Metric windows: use sliding windows for p95 and error-rate; avoid single-point anomalies by requiring sustained breach over 3 consecutive windows
Fallbacks: operator should support fast-failover to prior version via image tag or operator-mode switch rather than per-tenant full uninstall
Security: manifest signing key rotated via KMS; gating service verifies signature before acting
Backward compatibility: manifests must include 'required_api_semver' to prevent promoting controlplane versions that would break older private agents
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: terraform plan hook could block valid changes -> Mitigation: provide a dry-run-only mode and explicit human override with audit log
Risk: noisy metrics lead to flapping rollbacks -> Mitigation: smoothing windows, promotion cooldowns, and require multiple failing signals before rollback
Risk: state drift between tfstate and published manifest -> Mitigation: post-apply verification job that reconciles tfstate outputs to artifact registry and alerts on mismatch
